title: [v0.4.x] Roadmap: product readiness before the contract freeze
author: mcpdev80
body:
## Binding product correction — 2026-10-11

The updated #872 overrides conflicting older planning: **no migration scope before v1; no developer-supplied application IDs; no unconditional SQL/Secrets/Identity Core bundle; actual provider footprint follows requested capabilities plus genuine dependencies; complete ownership-safe add/remove/re-add lifecycle is required in v0.4.25.** Preserve shared consumers, data, recovery and security guarantees. A remaining fixed bundle or deferred capability-removal convergence blocks readiness.

#873/v0.4.26 adds the compact ONE-flow capability/provider wizard using the accepted foundation. It does not own missing backend lifecycle semantics. Later product scopes remain intact. v0.4.26 also includes the bounded workflow/CI V1 in #888: small task PRs against develop, conservative test selection and frozen release candidates. Only v0.4.25 retains the shared PR #881 on `work/v0.4.25-contract-minimal-core`. Earlier completion claims apply only to their narrower tested scope and do not satisfy this corrected contract.

## Purpose

Parent issue for the remaining BaseHarbor v0.4.x release line.

This line completes the product/runtime/developer contract before the v0.5 freeze.

Current release children: #872 (v0.4.25), #873 (v0.4.26), #874 (v0.4.27), #875 (v0.4.28), #876 (v0.4.29), #904 (v0.4.30), #174 (v0.4.31). Host-platform implementation #818/#819–#823 and audit #817 belong to #876; #777 belongs to #874. Quality #862 starts early and completes under #174. Published earlier v0.4.x work is historical, not outstanding scope.

Master roadmap: #155

## Host-resource preflight dependency

- #549 — host memory/resource preflight before provider and workload mutation.

Mutating runtime operations must evaluate host headroom before the first mutation and surface the same SAFE/WARN/FAIL semantics through human CLI, JSON and MCP.


## Network teardown dependency

- #550 — app/full destroy must remove BaseHarbor-owned runtime networks.

Network cleanup is part of the same ownership-safe teardown contract: BaseHarbor must not discard ownership/state before all provably owned runtime networks have been classified and cleaned up.


## Workload start reliability dependencies

- #250 — persisted workload-port fallback must be applied consistently during workload start/apply.
- #551 — repository workload start must fail fast on terminal runtime start errors.



## Capability-subset acceptance dependency

- #553 — reference demo config-matrix must prove valid capability subsets, mixed combinations and invalid cross-capability contracts.

The full-feature demo is not sufficient evidence that reduced Application Contracts converge correctly.


---

## Authoritative v0.4.25–v0.4.31 release split (2026-10-10)
Product scope below remains authoritative. The two-session/shared-branch model applies only to active v0.4.25. From v0.4.26, #888 replaces it with independent small task PRs against develop, required review/checks, conservative targeted tests and separately frozen candidates. Release qualification/promotion stays ordered; independent development may proceed in parallel. `#865–#871` remain assigned to **v0.4.24** and are not deferred.

| Release | Umbrella | Product area A | Product area B |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v0.4.25 | #872 | Minimal contract, system-owned IDs, provider/dependency resolution | Selective services, complete add/remove lifecycle, runtime acceptance |
| v0.4.26 | #873 + #888 | Greenfield/edit TUI and confirmation | CLI/JSON/MCP footprints and developer docs; bounded workflow/CI V1 |
| v0.4.27 | #874 | Node Connector, remote/Core/Target authority | #777 onboarding, portable profile and access |
| v0.4.28 | #875 | Console API/management integration | Console UX, full developer journeys |
| v0.4.29 | #876 | #819/#820/#821 Host seam, Linux, WSL2 | #822 Darwin/macOS, #823 conformance, #817 audit |
| v0.4.30 | #904 | Native TLS / justified proxies #902 | Attack protection baseline / DDoS boundaries #903 |
| v0.4.31 | #174 | Semantic/architecture/contract/security acceptance | #862 quality + final evidence/docs and freeze readiness |

Contract-semantic boundaries for later releases MUST be explicitly specified and pinned in **v0.4.25**, including #872's selective application/management dependency model (superseding the unconditional historical #810 bundle), minimal authored intent and system-generated stable ID, footprint v1 and Target provider-state ownership, #777 profile import/export, Host Platform seams, and machine-interface parity. Later releases consume these contracts and may fix behavior/implementation bugs without quietly redefining them. Formal compatibility freeze remains #175/v0.5, not v0.4.25.

Quality, safety, ownership, CLI/JSON/MCP parity, documentation, and exact-SHA scoped evidence are per-release requirements, not first introduced in v0.4.31. #862's static/vulnerability gates should be introduced as early as practical, then ratcheted across each release; final review is part of #174. The Console AI-assistant boundary must be explicitly decided before #175; no stealth deletion or unproven claim.

**Release-only stability cycle:** after v0.4.31 qualification and before #175, perform a dedicated no-new-features reconciliation of contract, release evidence, independent developer journeys, docs, compatibility/security and outstanding defects. No tagging/freeze until evidence and scope agree.

**Roadmap hygiene:** #155 is the master roadmap, #427 tracks productization, each #872–#876 owns its focused delivery, #174 is FINAL semantic acceptance in v0.4.31, and #175 owns v0.5 formal freeze. Parent references #777, #817–#823 and #862 follow this schedule. Older planning sections are historical and non-normative.

## Arbeitsmodell ab v0.4.26

#888 ist der verbindliche Umstellungsauftrag: kleine eigene Task-PRs gegen develop, konservative Testauswahl, lesbare CI und gefrorene Release-Kandidaten. Nach zwei instabilen Korrekturrunden bleibt eine sichere breitere Auswahl; kein Analyzer-Projekt als Blocker der Produktarbeit. Fremde PRs benötigen Marcels Review; eigene PRs die dokumentierte Solo-Ausnahme, alle PRs grüne Pflichtchecks. Regelwerk kurz und zentral; README ohne Prozessregeln.

Die gemeinsame Release-PR-/Zwei-Session-Regel gilt weiterhin ausschließlich für v0.4.25/#872/#881. #888 verändert dessen aktive Gates, Evidence und Freigaben nicht.
